What CAA Is Building Toward

The website isn't the mission. It's infrastructure for it.

Faith

Deepen your faith

Grow in your relationship with Christ and His Church, on the road as much as at home.

Fellowship

Never fly alone

Connect with Catholics across airports, airlines, and countries — real people, not a directory.

Flying

A calling worth investing in

From the beginning, CAA's mission has included affordable flight training and mentorship for the next generation of Catholic aviators — a vision we're building toward through local chapters and the Cupertino Aviation Clubs network.

Member Benefits

Member Story

A layover in Nairobi, a Mass I almost missed

By Marc Delacroix, First Officer · CAA Chapter — Dallas / Fort Worth

Ten minutes. That's all the layover left me between wheels-down and the van back to the crew hotel — and somehow it was enough.

I'd found St. Joseph Chapel through the CAA Mass finder two days earlier, half out of habit, half not expecting to actually use it. Terminal 3, daily Mass at 6:15 AM. I'd almost deleted the notification.

When the schedule changed and our layover shifted a day, I remembered it was there. I told the crew I'd catch the next van and walked the ten minutes across the terminal, still in uniform, rosary in my jacket pocket.

There were maybe fifteen people at that Mass. Two of them, it turned out, were also CAA members — a mechanic and a gate agent I'd never have met otherwise. We talked for five minutes afterward. I made the van.

That's the whole story. It isn't dramatic. But it's the reason I keep the app on my home screen, and the reason I tell every new hire on my crew to look up their layover cities before they need to.
